prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: corrected anatomical REAR VIEW animation atlas, 20 frames.
Reference image is ONLY the approved bear's color palette, fur rendering, and identity. The reference is viewed from in front. You must draw the OPPOSITE side of this animal: camera BEHIND its pelvis, looking along its back toward its shoulders and head.
Primary task: original painted chestnut grizzly bear sprites for a 1990s arcade style fantasy game. Anatomically coherent rear three-quarter view, walking away diagonally toward the UPPER RIGHT.
ANATOMY IS THE PRIORITY: one horizontal barrel-shaped torso; one broad rounded RUMP is CLOSEST to camera at lower left; a small SHORT TAIL protrudes from the center of that rump. Exactly two distinct HIND LEGS attach under the near pelvis, with natural hocks, broad rear paws and thighs. The shoulders/hump are FARTHER from camera, toward upper right. Exactly two FORELEGS attach there, under the distant chest. The head is farthest from camera, a small mostly hidden head beyond the shoulders, back of round ears visible. Only a tiny side edge of the muzzle may peek at far upper right. Correct overlap: near rump hides part of the belly and distant legs. Never place a giant front shoulder or an arm on the near rump. No extra limb-shaped fur columns. No backward-bending elbows. No human, ape, upright monster or gorilla anatomy. Do NOT take a front-facing body and merely turn the head away. All four legs belong to the SAME four-legged bear.
Design: warm chestnut and umber fur, honey highlights, short compact tail, small ears, chunky dark paws. Crisp hand-painted fur clusters and dark contours match the reference. Perspective about 20 degrees above the horizon, locked rear three-quarter angle in EVERY pose.
Layout: EXACTLY 4 columns x 5 rows, 20 isolated complete bears, left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Transparent background. Generous CLEAR gutters between drawings, no touching or overlapping adjacent cells, preserve all paws. Every pose same scale, no text or lines or shadows.
Row1 frames1-4: grounded neutral idle, slight breathing chest expansion/settle. Clear nearest rounded rump and two distinct planted rear paws. Normal quadruped bear, head facing away.
Row2 frames5-8: first half of eight-frame running lope AWAY: near hind-paw contact, weight acceptance, hind-leg drive, gathering under pelvis. Rear paws lift naturally, with soles briefly visible.
Row3 frames9-12: second half of the same run: opposite paw contact, acceptance, drive, gathering. Natural alternating four-limb sequence. Frame12 loops to5. Keep body weight horizontal and silhouette consistent.
Row4 frames13-16: claw attack AWAY from camera toward an opponent in front of the bear: load weight into near hindquarters; raise one DISTANT FRONT PAW at shoulder; swipe that forepaw forward toward upper right; recover to four feet. Rump stays closest, head remains farthest. Do not move attack paw onto a hind hip.
Row5 frames17-20: recoil from a hit; front knees buckle; torso rolls onto side; final collapsed bear resting on flank, still seen from behind with rump and back closest and head at far upper right. No blood.
Output one transparent PNG. The result must look like a real grizzly seen FROM BEHIND, with clear rump/tail/two hind legs and distant shoulders, in every frame.
